title: "Figure 4—figure supplement (number pending, PROVISIONAL) — does the closed-form Fisher reproduce the differenced one? The analytic Gaussian Fisher against the numerical Fisher, in size and in shape"

<!--
PROVISIONAL, and not a candidate for the paper in this state. The two members the question is about
are the two this figure cannot draw. Read the coverage note below before reading the maps.

THE QUESTION, which is about the DEVICE and not about calibration. Every distortion in this set is
built on a Fisher information, and there are two ways to get one: the closed-form Gaussian
expression, which is cheap, and differencing the likelihood, which is not. If they agree the cheap
one can be used everywhere and the whole set rests on it. If they do not, every figure anchored on
the analytic Fisher inherits the gap. This asks how far apart they are, with the same two numbers
the magnitude/anisotropy supplement uses, because "how far apart are two positive definite
matrices" is the same question there and here.

WHAT IT IS. Two panels over the same plane, five members, one column each, 10 columns, both reading
Likelihood_Gaussian_Fisher_Distortion = inv(sqrt(G_b)) * F_b * inv(sqrt(G_b)), with G_b the analytic
Gaussian Fisher and F_b the finite-difference one:

  A  size    exp(mean(log lambda)), the typical factor by which the analytic formula misses. Below
             1 it understates the information the differenced likelihood carries, above 1 it
             overstates it.
  B  shape   exp(sd(log lambda)), whether it misses by the same factor in every direction. At 1 the
             analytic Fisher is the numerical one up to a scalar and could be rescaled; above 1 the
             two matrices differ in a way no rescaling reaches.

Same scale as everything else in the set, one bar, criteria 1.15 and 2, CI-aware toward 1.

THE COVERAGE, and it is why this is provisional. The quantity exists only in the NON-`_G` runs: the
`_G` sweep is gaussian-only, F_b is never formed there, and the slot is `nan` in all 240 cells.
What the non-`_G` runs have at nsim 10000 is NR, R, MR, NMR and IR at three noise levels, 0.1, 1
and 10, against the nine to twelve the rest of the set reaches. Absent entirely: least squares,
which is the member the analytic Fisher is reported to fail for, and INR, which is the high-noise
comparison. So the figure today shows the members for which the answer was already expected to be
yes, and is silent on both cases.

NMR IS SUPERSEDED. These runs predate the fix at HEAD that restored the interval conductance
variance in the non-recursive path and renamed the member INR, so this column is the version
missing the N*ms term. It is drawn because it carries by far the largest departure in the file and
that is worth seeing, and it must be labelled superseded in any caption.

WHAT IT SHOWS, medians over the seven intervals, POOL anchor, as factors:

               noise 0.1                        noise 10
      N_ch:    10     100    1e3    1e4      10     100    1e3    1e4
 size  NR     1.007  1.010  1.264  1.602    1.001  1.011  1.016  1.005
       NMR    1.005  1.003  1.585  2.307    1.002  1.002  1.006  1.003
       R      1.028  1.017  1.009  1.001    1.009  1.006  1.005  1.012
       MR     1.041  1.030  1.012  1.002    1.018  1.020  1.022  1.021
       IR     1.014  1.004  1.000  1.000    1.002  0.999  1.000  1.000
 shape NR     1.093  1.044  1.885  3.103    1.075  1.034  1.041  1.038
       NMR    1.027  1.015  2.687  6.216    1.064  1.022  1.026  1.020
       R      1.055  1.026  1.018  1.011    1.043  1.027  1.029  1.027
       MR     1.097  1.049  1.025  1.010    1.083  1.047  1.048  1.048
       IR     1.033  1.011  1.003  1.003    1.038  1.008  1.004  1.004

THE CLOSED FORM IS THE DIFFERENCED ONE FOR EVERY RECURSIVE MEMBER, everywhere on this plane: R, MR
and IR sit within 4 per cent in size and 10 in shape at every cell, and IR within half a per cent
once there are a thousand channels. So the analytic Fisher the rest of the set rests on is not
adding anything of its own for those members, which is the result this figure exists to state.

IT FAILS FOR THE TWO OPEN-LOOP MEMBERS, and in one corner of the plane: NR and NMR at LOW noise,
LONG sampling interval and MANY channels. NR reads 1.26 and 1.60 in size at a thousand and ten
thousand channels at noise 0.1, NMR 1.58 and 2.31, and at noise 1 NMR is still 1.59 at ten thousand
while everything else has recovered. The interval is the axis the medians hide and the map shows:
the departure is a wedge opening toward the long intervals, and it widens down the channel count
until at ten thousand it has taken most of the row. All three directions are the same direction,
deeper into where the data is least Gaussian, which is what a moment-matched closed form should do
when it leaves the regime it was matched in.

SHAPE FAILS HARDER THAN SIZE, in every cell where anything fails: 3.10 against 1.60 for NR, 6.22
against 2.31 for NMR, 2.70 against 1.59 at noise 1. So where the analytic Fisher misses, it is not
missing by a factor that could be divided out; the two matrices differ in direction. That is the
argument for drawing the pair rather than one number, and it is the same argument the
magnitude/anisotropy supplement makes about the distortion.

THE ANCHOR MATTERS HERE AND IT IS WORTH RECORDING. At theta_sim the same medians read 0.86 to 0.93
in size for R and 1.15 to 1.42 in shape, against 1.00 to 1.03 and 1.01 to 1.06 at theta_pool: the
recursive members look 6 to 15 per cent off at the simulation truth and agree at the optimum. That
is the expected signature of a differenced Hessian evaluated off the maximum rather than of a real
disagreement between the two Fishers, and it is an argument for the pool anchor being the right
default for THIS question, whatever it is for the distortion.

THE PLANE IS THREE NOISE LEVELS TALL, which is what makes this figure look unlike its siblings.
Every other map in the set spans nine to twelve decades of noise; this one spans two, four times
over. The geometry is calibrated for that and not borrowed.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# The five members with a non-_G run, in ladder order: the sample level instantaneous and interval,
# then the recursive level instantaneous and partially corrected, then the complete one.
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("macro_NR", "macro_NMR", "macro_R", "macro_MR", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(macro_NR = "NR", macro_NMR = "NMR*", macro_R = "R",
                    macro_MR = "MR", macro_IR = "IR")
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/433ed13", "../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6",
                    "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b")
FIG4_PARS   <- c("mag", "aniso")
FIG4_PSHORT <- c(mag = "'size'", aniso = "'shape'")
source("figure_4_common.R")
# The independent builder, and then the re-point: the layout reads its plane out of `bias`, `stat`
# and GRID_BY_ALGO, all of which describe the _G grid until this runs. Between the two sources is
# the only place it can go.
source("figure_4_fisher_data.R")
fis <- dplyr::filter(fisher_source_data(), anchor == ANCHOR, algo %in% ALGOS,
                     is.finite(Sconf), Sconf > 0)
fisher_repoint(fis)
source("figure_4_layout.R")
cat("fisher cells: ", nrow(fis), " rows, noise levels ",
    paste(sort(unique(fis$noise)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r sides}
# Neither side declares a scale, so both take SCALE_FACTOR and the render gives them one bar: the
# two are commensurable by construction, being the two orthogonal parts of one distance.
SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "size: how far the closed form misses", letter = "A",
       data = dplyr::filter(fis, param == "mag"),   zf = function(x) log10(x$Sconf)),
  list(lab = "shape: whether it misses evenly", letter = "B",
       data = dplyr::filter(fis, param == "aniso"), zf = function(x) log10(x$Sconf)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.4, fig.height = 3.67}
# 10 columns over two sides, no key row and no white contours. per_row 0.3510, x 0.2823, y 0.2823,
# 100.0 per cent, cell 2.05 mm.
#
# SOLVED ON THE REAL FIGURE and not in tmp/calib_fig4.R, because this plane is 8 decades of noise
# against the set's 27.204 (three levels, 0.1 to 10, over four N_ch rows) and no case in that file
# has this geometry. The figure is cheap enough to iterate on directly: render, read the printed
# isotropy per cent, multiply per_row by 100/that, repeat. It took two rounds from 0.320.
# The page is 3.67 in, the shortest in the set, and that is the coverage showing: two decades of
# noise per row cannot fill more.
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = 0.3510, out = "Figure_4_supplement_gaussian_vs_numeric_fisher.pdf",
            se_lines = FALSE, key = FALSE)
```

```{r table}
# the medians in the note, rebuilt from the source so the two cannot drift
fis %>%
  dplyr::group_by(param, algo, noise, Num_ch) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(v = median(m), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(algo = factor(ALGO_LAB[algo], levels = ALGO_LAB[ALGOS]),
                param = factor(param, levels = c("mag", "aniso"))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Num_ch, values_from = v) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(param, noise, algo) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  print(digits = 4)
```
